newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks bounce back strongly.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks bounce back strongly.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks clawed back part of the previous day's big losses Thursday as investors focused on corporate earnings, which have been mostly upbeat so far in the second-quarter reporting period.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended up 44.33 points at 7,886.76 after Wednesday's 120-point loss.
The Nasdaq Composite index rolled to its sixth consecutive record, gaining 4.30 points to 1,490.93.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,764 to 1,038 on heavy volume of 551 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Blue chips were again buoyed by solid earnings news, this time from General Electric Co., which reported a record profit of $2.16 billion in the second quarter. GE climbed 1-1/16 to 69-1/2.
The early earnings returns, particularly from blue chip companies, had some analysts voicing optimism about the quarter.

"Most of the negative feelings that existed coming into this quarter seemed to centre on fears of higher interest rates and the impact of a too-strong dollar," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Kemper Funds. "Neither of those really developed."

Technology stocks continued their torrid streak, overcoming a weak showing by computer chip bellwether Intel Corp., which fell 2-1/2 to 150-1/8 after Salomon Brothers voiced caution about the company's upcoming results.
Investors opted to focus on the bigger picture, however, looking past Intel's problems, which largely involve issues related to its transition to a new generation of chips.

For now, the broader view is a fairly rosy one. Of the 96 companies reporting earnings through Thursday, 54.2 percent have beaten expectations, while only 29.2 have fallen short of estimates, according to Zacks Investment Research.
The pace of earnings surprises is off slightly from a year ago, which several analysts noted reflected high expectations in the market.

"It doesn't appear we're going to have quite as big a surprise factor," said Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker. "That could take away some of the momentum that had been created in the market."
The result could be more of the choppy, sideways activity that has gripped the Dow index since its sizzling 223-point run heading into the July 4 Independence Day holiday.
Since that time, the blue chip average has swung wildly, gyrating in 100-point or larger bands in each session, all while giving up a total of only 9 points.
"I think if we head into a period of back-and-forth consolidation, it would be a positive for this market," Cripps said. "We had such a huge move, it's reasonable to see the market take a rest."
Within the sideways market, pockets of furious activity continue to surface.
International Paper Co. surged 3-1/16 to 58, extending a rally since the company reported stronger-than-expected earnings and announced a restructuring Tuesday.
Wal-Mart Stores Inc. rose 1-7/16 to 35-1/16. The giant retailer was one of several to report strong June sales, with comparable-store sales up 6.4 percent in the month.
Marvel Entertainment Group Inc. rose 1/8 to 2-3/8 after it reached agreement on a merger with Toy Biz Inc.
The deal, which was approved by Marvel's banks and bondholders, may spell an end to months of bitter litigation and enable Marvel to emerge from bankruptcy by fall. Toy Biz jumped 1-5/16 to 9-5/16.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 6.24 points to 913.78. The American Stock Exchange index edged up 0.68 to 631.70.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 3.24 to 476.27. The average share was up 30 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 8,642.279, up 50.879, or 0.59 percent.
